cards.explanation: The answer is that they both fall into a pit. Jesus asks, "Will they not both fall into a pit?" (Luke 6:39). The question lands on both of them, not just one. That's what makes it such a sharp picture, friends.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "A disciple is not above his teacher…" (Luke 6:40). The learner isn't over the one teaching him. A disciple is a learner following a teacher, and that's the order Jesus gives, friends.

The answer is his teacher. Jesus says, "…everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher." (Luke 6:40). Fully trained is the key, friends. A disciple who finishes his training becomes like the one who taught him.

The answer is beam. A speck is tiny, and a beam is a big heavy piece of timber. Jesus sets them side by side in Luke 6:41, and the size gap is the whole picture. It's like a single sprinkle next to a full oven rack, and somebody's only worried about the sprinkle.

The answer is a hypocrite. Jesus says, "You hypocrite!" (Luke 6:42). He's talking to someone who offers to help his brother with a speck while he can't see the beam in his own eye. It's a word for somebody whose offer doesn't match his own situation, friends.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye." (Luke 6:42). Notice the order, friends. Your own eye comes first, and then you can see clearly to help your brother.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit." (Luke 6:43). It goes both directions, friends. Good trees and their fruit match, and so do bad trees and theirs.

The answer is fruit. Jesus says, "For each tree is known by its own fruit." (Luke 6:44). What a tree grows tells you what kind of tree it is, friends. Then He adds that figs aren't gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

The answer is the good treasure of his heart. Jesus says, "The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart…" (Luke 6:45). The source is his heart, friends. What comes out of him starts there.

The answer is heart. Jesus says, "For out of the overflow of the heart the mouth speaks." (Luke 6:45). Picture a mixing bowl filled to the top, friends. Whatever's inside is what spills over, and in this verse that spill is what the mouth says.

The answer is that they don't do what He says. Jesus asks, "Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?" (Luke 6:46). Saying the words and doing what He says are two different things, friends. I think that question lands softly and still hits hard.

The answer is a man building a house. Jesus says the one who comes to Him, hears His words and acts on them is "…like a man building a house…" (Luke 6:48). It's a builder's picture, friends. And a builder is somebody who's actually doing something.

The answer is rock. Jesus says the man "…dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock." (Luke 6:48). He didn't skip the digging and he didn't stop early, friends. The rock is where the house sits.

The answer is False. Jesus says the torrent "…crashed against that house but could not shake it…" (Luke 6:48). It hit hard, and the house didn't move. The flood really came and the house still held, friends.

The answer is that it was well built. Jesus says the torrent "…could not shake it, because it was well built." (Luke 6:48). The text gives that reason, friends. The house stood because of how it was built, right down to the foundation on the rock.

The answer is foundation. Jesus says this man "…built his house on ground without a foundation." (Luke 6:49). The first builder dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock, friends. This one skipped that part.
The answer is that it falls right away. Jesus says, "The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell…" (Luke 6:49). No leaning and no waiting around, friends. It went down right away.
